column1: # *** AND NOW THE TWO WHO ARE NOT THERE. ***
# *** ISABELLA TEMPLE, who would be 16, and MARY SEPTIMA, who would be 6, are ABSENT from their
# parents' house on census night. ***
# Isabella at sixteen is easy: *** her brother was in service at nineteen and her sister was a
# "mother's help" at twenty ***, so a girl of sixteen from this household would very likely be living
# in somebody else's. *** Mary Septima at SIX is not easy at all. ***
# *** A COUNTY-WIDE CHECK WAS RUN: *** every Taylor born 1882-1886 in FreeCEN's Devon for 1891 - 368
# people - and *** there is no Mary Septima and no Mary S. anywhere in it. ***
# *** THE NULL IS SOFT AND MUST BE READ AS SOFT. *** FreeCEN's Devon is transcribed parish by parish
# and 1891 is not complete for the county - Northam is, which is why the household above is whole.
# *** So what this establishes is narrow and real: she is not in NORTHAM in 1891. Where she was is now
# an open question, and it was not one before tonight. ***
# *** WHAT IT DOES TO THE "EDITH" CANDIDATE - WEAKENED, NOT KILLED. ***
# Row 127 was opened because the tree says TEN children, names nine, and *** "Septima" means seventh ***.
# The birth index offered *** TAYLOR, Edith, Bideford, Sep quarter 1882 *** and this archive
# independently knew Mary Septima stayed with *** her sister EDIE *** at 26 Fore Street, Northam, in 1935.
# *** There is no Edith of that age in Northam in 1891. *** The only Edith Taylor in the parish was born
# at Cardiff in 1886 and is somebody else's.
# *** BUT THE CENSUS CANNOT CARRY THAT ARGUMENT VERY FAR, because MARY SEPTIMA IS MISSING FROM IT TOO ***
# - and a household return cannot distinguish a child who was elsewhere from a child who never existed.
# *** AND THERE IS A THIRD READING THAT FITS EVERYTHING: a child who died before 1891 would appear in
# the birth index, be counted in the family's ten, and never reach a census at all. ***
# *** So the count still demands a seventh daughter and the archive still has none. Graded OPEN. ***
# ============ AND TWO MORE BRAYLEYS IN THE SAME PARISH, FOUND BY CHANGING THE SPELLING ============
# *** The household above was found by searching TAYLOR. Searching BRAYLEY in the same parish and year
# finds two more people, and one of them is the grandmother. ***
# *** A search under BRAILEY returns ZERO for Devon in 1891 *** - the household that was BRAILEY in 1861
# is BRAYLEY again by 1891. *** Fourth spelling trap of the evening. ***
who
*** GEORGINA BRAYLEY *** , the Scotswoman
column2: *** THE ALMS HOUSE, NORTHAM *** - piece 1787, ED 6, folio 72, page 6, schedule 40
column3: *** Head, WIDOW, 77, "LIVING ON MEANS", born Scotland, EAST LOTHIAN. Living alone. ***
column4: *** THIS IS GEORGINA TEMPLE AT THE END, AND IT COMPLETES A SENTENCE THE TREE ONLY HALF-WROTE. *** The tree gives her occupation as *** "Monthly Nurse & Shoemaker Wife Pauper" *** , which has always read like three things run together. *** Here is the third: an alms house. *** Follow her across four records and the whole life is there - *** "Shoemaker Wife" in 1851, a married lodger in her father-in-law's house with her husband five weeks from dying in the county asylum; "Mangles Clothes" in 1861, a widow keeping her own household; the ALMS HOUSE in 1891; and a death at Bideford in the March quarter of 1900, aged 85. *** *** And she is in NORTHAM, the same parish as her daughter's family at 2 Fore Street - a different enumeration district and a short walk. *** Her age, 77 in April 1891, agrees with a birth on 23 August 1814 at Haddington. *** The Scottish end of the ascent is now on four English records. ***

column1: *** GEORGINA BRAYLEY *** , aged 20
column2: *** TOWER STREET, NORTHAM *** - piece 1787, ED 3, folio 36, page 21, schedule 107
column3: *** Servant, single, 20, GENERAL SERVANT, born MIDDLESEX, LONDON KILBURN *** - in the household of Thomas LOCK, 51, widower, Draper (Employer), of Northam, and his daughter Fanny E. Lock, 24.
column4: *** A CANDIDATE PERSON, AND GRADED AS A CANDIDATE. *** A Brayley, born in London about 1871, in service in Northam - *** which is precisely the pattern of Mary Ann Hellen herself, who was a "House Servant" in a china dealer's house at Bideford in 1861 at eighteen. *** And the forename is the family's: *** Georgina Temple's name is carried by Georgina Margaret (1850) and Kathleen Georgina (1870). *** *** THE OBVIOUS READING IS THAT SHE IS A GRANDDAUGHTER OF GEORGINA TEMPLE, most likely a daughter of JOHN WALKER BRAYLEY *** , who was born in London, was 26 in 1871, and whose own birthplace the records give as St Pancras. *** NONE OF THAT IS PROVEN HERE. *** The census states no relationship to anybody in this family. *** What would settle it: her birth in the index, London, about 1871, under Brayley or Brailey - and whether John Walker Brayley married. ***
